mainTopic: When יום הכפורים and an אשם תלוי do not cancel a חטאת; the doubtful bird חטאת; and rams bought with money set aside for an אשם
overview: The amud opens by finishing the rejection of a proof from the נשיא, whose קרבן can change. אביי then shows that the extra mentions of 'knowing the sin' teach that someone who finds out after יום הכפורים still brings a חטאת. רבא adds that a פסוק requires the חטאת even after an אשם תלוי. The גמרא explains that the אשם תלוי protects a person from suffering until then. Next, the גמרא discusses a bird חטאת brought out of doubt. It concludes that the משנה's burial rule applies when she learns she did not give birth, and that the burial is מדרבנן. רב and רבי יוחנן then argue over whether the bird may be eaten when she learns after מליקה that she did give birth, and each side has a supporting ברייתא. Finally, a new משנה deals with two rams bought with two סלעים set aside for an אשם. The גמרא asks what 'his מעילה' means and finds the רישא and סיפא seem to use the word differently, a question that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The proof from the נשיא is rejected
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes rejecting the previous proof, because a נשיא is a special case whose קרבן can change.
steps.simpleTranslation: [How can you learn this] from a נשיא, whose קרבן is liable to change?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its rejection of an earlier attempt to find a source. That attempt relied on a verse about the נשיא, and the גמרא says the נשיא is too unusual to learn from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נשיא's קרבן is not fixed. If he loses his position, he brings the קרבן of a regular person instead. Because his status is unstable, a rule learned from his case cannot be applied to everyone, so the earlier proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: The leader or king, who brings a special חטאת (a male goat)
Liable to change; his special status and korban can switch

phrases.english: with regard to a נשיא, who is liable to change!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the rejection of the earlier proof, which came just before this section
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The previous source, which was based on the נשיא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A נשיא's korban can change, so his case is not a solid base for a general rule

steps.title: אביי's new source: the three cases are linked
steps.stepSummary: אביי starts a new proof. The word 'מצות' links the חטאת of the יחיד, the נשיא and the צבור, so each case teaches the others.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: [we learn it] from here. Since 'מצות' and 'מצות' are learned from one another...
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers a fresh source in place of the rejected one. He starts by laying down a premise; the actual proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'מצות' appears in the פרשיות of the יחיד, the נשיא and the צבור. Because of this shared word (a גזירה שוה), any rule stated in one case applies to the others. That premise will soon show that some verses are extra.

keyTerms.meaning: Since / now consider: introduces a known premise
The word 'commandments', which appears in all three חטאת parshiyos
They are learned from one another
A link between verses based on a shared word

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said: from here:
Since 'מצוות' and 'מצוות' are derived from one another,
phrases.notes: See ויקרא 4:13, 4:22 and 4:27, where the word מצות appears for the צבור, the נשיא and the יחיד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected proof with a new source
steps.raayaObject: That a later-discovered sin still needs a חטאת even after יום הכפורים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The גזירה שוה of 'מצות' linking the three חטאת parshiyos

steps.title: The extra 'knowing' verses teach the יום הכפורים case
steps.stepSummary: Since the three cases teach each other, mentioning 'knowing' three times is extra. So the extra mentions teach that someone who finds out after יום הכפורים still brings a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since they are learned from one another, why does the Torah write 'knowing' three times, for the יחיד, the נשיא and the צבור? If it is not needed for its own subject, because the 'מצות' link already teaches it, apply it to the case where he finds out after יום הכפורים: he still brings a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי completes his proof. The repeated phrase about 'the sin becoming known' is extra, so it must teach something new: יום הכפורים does not cancel the חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One mention of 'knowing' would have been enough, because the 'מצות' link spreads it to all three cases. The extra mentions are reassigned to a new lesson using the rule of אם אינו ענין. The new lesson: even if יום הכפורים passed before he found out, he must still bring a חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: Knowing: the sinner becoming aware of his sin
If it is not needed for its own subject, so the verse is extra
Apply it to a different subject
Sin offering, brought for a definite accidental sin

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, the Torah's repeated mention of 'knowing the sin' teaches that יום הכפורים does not exempt a person from his חטאת if he finds out about the sin afterward.

phrases.english: Since they are derived from one another,
why do I need it to be written three times about knowing
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:14, 4:23 and 4:28 each speak of the sin becoming known.

phrases.aramaic: גַּבֵּי יָחִיד וְגַבֵּי נָשִׂיא וְגַבֵּי צִבּוּר?
phrases.english: for an individual, for a Nasi, and for the community?
If it is not needed for their own matter,
since they are already learned through 'מצוות' and 'מצוות',

phrases.aramaic: תְּנֵהוּ עִנְיָן הֵיכָא דְּמִתְיְידַע לֵיהּ בָּתַר יוֹם הַכִּיפּוּרִים
phrases.english: apply it to the case where it becomes known to him after Yom Kippur:
that he brings a sin offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּיָלְפִי מֵהֲדָדֵי, לְמָה לִי דִּכְתִיב שָׁלֹשׁ יְדִיעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the premise from step 2 to finish אביי's proof
steps.raayaObject: A person who learns of his sin after יום הכפורים still brings a חטאת
steps.raayaSupportSource: The extra mentions of 'knowing' in the three חטאת parshiyos
steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes the base for the next question: does the same rule apply after an אשם תלוי?

steps.title: Maybe an אשם תלוי is different from יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges whether the rule carries over. יום הכפורים was not brought for this specific sin, but an אשם תלוי was, so maybe it fully atones and no חטאת is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that only when he finds out after יום הכפורים does he bring a חטאת, because יום הכפורים did not come for this sin. But an אשם תלוי, which does come for this sin, perhaps really does atone. So if he finds out after bringing an אשם תלוי, he would not bring a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: אביי's source proves the rule for יום הכפורים, but maybe not for an אשם תלוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יום הכפורים atones in a general way and was not aimed at this sin, so it makes sense that it does not cancel the חטאת. An אשם תלוי, by contrast, was brought for exactly this doubtful sin. Perhaps it gives full atonement, and then the person would not need a חטאת when he later finds out.

keyTerms.meaning: Say / perhaps: introduces a counter-suggestion
Provisional guilt offering, brought when unsure whether one sinned
He has received atonement
It comes for this specific sin

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two קרבנות. An אשם תלוי is for a sin you are not sure about; a חטאת is for a sin you are sure about. The question is whether the first one, already brought, covers you once you become sure.

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא כִּי מִתְיְידַע לֵיהּ בָּתַר יוֹם כִּפּוּרִים
phrases.english: Say that when it becomes known to him after Yom Kippur
he brings a sin offering,

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים לָאו עַל הָדֵין חֵטְא קָא אָתֵי,
phrases.english: because Yom Kippur does not come for this specific sin,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אָשָׁם תָּלוּי, דְּעַל הָדֵין חֵטְא קָאָתֵי,
phrases.english: but a provisional guilt offering, which does come for this sin,
say that indeed he has received atonement,

phrases.aramaic: דְּכִי מִתְיְידַע [לֵיהּ] לְבָתַר דְּקָא מַיְיתֵי אָשָׁם תָּלוּי
phrases.english: so that if it becomes known to him after he brought a provisional guilt offering,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is not in every version, but the meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: he does not bring a sin offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא כִּי מִתְיְידַע לֵיהּ בָּתַר יוֹם כִּפּוּרִים הוּא דְּמַיְיתֵי חַטָּאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether אביי's proof about יום הכפורים also applies to an אשם תלוי
steps.kashyaTarget: Using אביי's source to show that a חטאת is still needed after an אשם תלוי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יום הכפורים is general and not aimed at this sin, while an אשם תלוי targets this exact sin and so might fully atone

steps.title: A verse says the חטאת is brought in any case
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers the challenge from a פסוק: whenever the sin becomes known, a חטאת is brought, even after an אשם תלוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The פסוק says 'or if it be known to him.' That means in any case, even after an אשם תלוי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge from the last step. A פסוק shows that once the sin becomes known, a חטאת is required no matter what.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge said the אשם תלוי was brought for this very sin, so maybe it already atoned fully. רבא says the words 'או הודע אליו' include every case where the person finds out. So an earlier אשם תלוי does not cancel the חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Or if it be known to him': the פסוק about finding out about one's sin
In any case, with no exceptions
Provisional guilt offering, brought when a person is unsure whether he sinned

phrases.english: Rava said: The verse states:
"Or if it be known to him" – in any case.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבא אמר קרא או הודע אליו מכל מקום
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 4 that the אשם תלוי may fully atone.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Scriptural inclusion: the verse's wording covers every case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The אשם תלוי, brought for this exact sin, might fully atone and cancel the חטאת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק requires a חטאת whenever the sin becomes known, even after an אשם תלוי.

steps.title: So what is the אשם תלוי for?
steps.stepSummary: If a חטאת is brought anyway once he finds out, the גמרא asks what purpose the אשם תלוי serves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you say he brings a חטאת when he finds out, why does he bring an אשם תלוי at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts רבא's answer but asks a follow-up question: what is the אשם תלוי for, if it does not exempt him from the חטאת?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 showed the אשם תלוי does not replace the חטאת. So the גמרא wants to know what the אשם תלוי actually does. This sets up the next two answers.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that you say: building a question on what was just established
It becomes known to him

phrases.english: Now that you say:
when it becomes known to him he brings a sin offering,
why does a provisional guilt offering come?

steps.triggerLanguage: השתא דאמר כי מתיידע ליה מייתי חטאת אשם תלוי למה בא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 5's conclusion that a חטאת is still required.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the אשם תלוי accomplish if it does not exempt from a חטאת?

steps.title: רבי זירא: in case he dies first
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says the אשם תלוי makes sure that if he dies before finding out, he dies free of sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: So that if he dies, he dies without sin.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers: the אשם תלוי protects the person in case he dies before he ever finds out and brings a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי זירא, the אשם תלוי gives temporary atonement. It covers him until the חטאת, so death in between would not leave him with sin.

keyTerms.meaning: Dies without sin, with nothing left to atone for

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said: So that if he dies,
he dies without iniquity.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי זירא שאם מת מת בלא עון
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The אשם תלוי protects him from dying with the sin.

steps.title: רבא: death itself atones
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects that death wipes away sin by itself, so an אשם תלוי is not needed for that.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected: If he dies, death itself cleans away sin!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רבי זירא's answer. If the person dies, his death already atones, so the אשם תלוי adds nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא's reason only works if death leaves sin in place. רבא points out that death itself is a form of atonement. So 'in case he dies' cannot be the purpose of the אשם תלוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Objects to it: a sage challenges a statement
Death cleanses away sin

phrases.english: Rava objects to it:
If he dies, death absolves!

steps.triggerLanguage: מתקיף לה רבא מת מיתה ממרקת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי זירא's answer in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's explanation that the אשם תלוי protects one who dies
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Death itself atones, so no offering is needed to protect a person who dies.

steps.title: רבא: it protects him from suffering
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives his own reason: the אשם תלוי shields the person from suffering until he brings his חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: It is to protect him from suffering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a new answer. The אשם תלוי protects the person from suffering during his lifetime, before he finds out about the sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since death already atones, the protection must be for while he is alive. Until the חטאת comes, the אשם תלוי keeps punishment in the form of suffering away from him.

keyTerms.meaning: Suffering that comes as a punishment for sin
To protect him

steps.whatToRemember: An אשם תלוי does not cancel the חטאת. According to רבא, it protects the person from suffering until he finds out and brings the חטאת.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
to protect him from suffering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא אמר רבא להגן עליו מן הייסורים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבי זירא's rejected answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New explanation replacing a rejected one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The אשם תלוי protects one who dies before finding out.
steps.terutzMaskana: The אשם תלוי protects him from suffering in his lifetime.

steps.title: רב: the doubtful bird חטאת atoned
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a bird חטאת brought out of doubt, and רב says it atoned.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה speaks of a bird חטאת brought because of a doubt. רב said: and it atoned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes the משנה about a doubtful bird חטאת, and רב says that once she found out she really was obligated, the bird had already atoned for her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes at first that 'it became known to her' means she found out she definitely had a birth that requires a קרבן. רב rules that the bird still counted and atoned. This sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird brought as a חטאת
Brought because of a doubt
And it atoned

phrases.english: A bird sin offering that is brought due to uncertainty.
Rav says: And it atoned.

steps.triggerLanguage: חטאת העוף הבא על הספק אמר רב וכיפר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new section on another line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A doubtful bird חטאת atones once she learns she was obligated.

steps.title: If it atoned, why bury it?
steps.stepSummary: If the bird atoned, it should be eaten like a normal חטאת. So why does the משנה say to bury it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why must it be buried?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב. A bird חטאת that atoned is normally eaten by the כהנים, so burying it does not fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the bird turned out to be a real, working חטאת, its meat should go to the כהנים. The משנה's ruling of burial suggests it was not a real חטאת, which clashes with רב.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: if what was just said is true
It must be buried

phrases.english: If so, why must it be buried?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's statement in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that the bird atoned
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An atoning bird חטאת is eaten by the כהנים, yet the משנה requires burial.

steps.title: It was not guarded
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the bird must be buried because it was not watched, so it may have become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it was not guarded.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב. The bird is buried because nobody watched over it, so it might have become טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a doubtful bird is normally not eaten, the כהן did not bother to watch it. That raises a worry of טומאה, which would explain the burial even though the bird atoned.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not guarded, so it might have become טמא

phrases.english: Because it is not guarded.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical reason for burial that does not deny atonement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Burial means the bird did not work as a חטאת.
steps.terutzMaskana: Burial is because of a worry of טומאה from lack of guarding.

steps.title: When was it ever unguarded?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the answer: before מליקה the bird was alive and cannot become טמא, and after מליקה the כהן guards it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When was it not guarded? If at the start, it was alive! If at the end, he guards it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer of step 12. There is no time when the bird was both open to טומאה and left unguarded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before its neck was pinched, the bird was alive, and a living creature does not become טמא. After the pinching, the כהן already watches it. So the 'not guarded' answer falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: When?
At the start
At the end

phrases.english: When is it not guarded?
If at the outset – it was alive!
phrases.notes: A living bird can't become טמא, so there was nothing to guard yet.

phrases.english: If later – he is guarding it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אימת לא משתמרת אי מעיקרא חיה הויא אי לבסוף קמנטר לה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the bird was left unguarded
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: At every stage, either the bird cannot become טמא or it is being guarded.

steps.title: She found out she never gave birth, so burial is rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the משנה: she learned she did not give birth, so the bird is really ordinary and permitted, and burial is only a rabbinic rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the משנה is where she found out she did not give birth. By right the bird is permitted for benefit. And what does 'it must be buried' mean? Only by rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up its first reading of the משנה. The case is where she found out there was no birth, so the bird was never a real korban, and the burial rule is only מדרבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since no explanation of burial works if she really was obligated, the גמרא changes the case. If she was never obligated, the bird is ordinary and could even be used. The חכמים required burial anyway, so people won't think benefit from a doubtful bird חטאת is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Permitted to benefit from
By rabbinic law, not from the תורה
By strict law, it should really be

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's case is a woman who found out she never gave birth. By תורה law the bird is permitted, but the חכמים require it to be buried.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'it became known to her' as 'she found out she was obligated.' The גמרא ends up explaining it the other way: she found out she was NOT obligated.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מַתְנִיתִין בְּנוֹדַע לָהּ דְּלֹא יָלְדָה,
phrases.english: Rather, the mishna is where it became known to her that she did not give birth,
and by right it is permitted to derive benefit from it,
and what is "it must be buried"? By rabbinic law.

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא מתניתין בנודע לה דלא ילדה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 13 knocks out the 'unguarded' answer, the גמרא redefines the case of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה speaks of a woman who learned she was obligated, so the bird atoned.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה speaks of a woman who learned she was not obligated. The bird is permitted by תורה law and buried only מדרבנן.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Burial of the doubtful bird חטאת is a rabbinic rule, in the case where she learned she did not give birth.

steps.title: רב's ruling was said about a different case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves רב's statement to a different case: a woman who brought a bird חטאת out of doubt and then found out she definitely gave birth. First it reviews the rule for when she finds out before מליקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב's statement was said, it was about this case: a woman brought a bird חטאת out of doubt. If, before the bird was pinched, she found out she definitely gave birth, she makes it a definite חטאת. The same kind of bird she brings when she is unsure is the kind she brings when she is sure.
steps.whatsHappening: Step 14 explained the משנה as a woman who found out she did NOT give birth, so רב's 'it atoned' cannot belong there. The גמרא therefore moves רב's statement to a different case, and first states the rule for finding out before מליקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 11-14 struggled to explain why a bird that atoned should be buried. Now the גמרא says רב was talking about a woman who found out she DID give birth. Here the bird really is a proper חטאת, so saying it atoned makes simple sense. If she finds out before מליקה, the bird simply becomes a definite חטאת, because a doubtful and a definite bird חטאת are the same kind of קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: And when it was said: it introduces the true place of an earlier statement
Doubt; brought when it is not clear she is obligated
Definite, certain
Was pinched at the back of the neck (מליקה), the way a bird korban is killed
Unknown / known: being unsure versus being sure

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with Step 14's case. There she found out she did NOT give birth. Here she found out she DEFINITELY gave birth, a totally different case.

phrases.english: And when the statement of Rav was said,
phrases.notes: He means רב's ruling from Step 10, that the bird atoned.

phrases.english: it was about the woman who brought
a bird sin offering out of doubt:
if before it was pinched
she found out that she definitely gave birth,
she should make it a definite sin offering,
because from the same kind she brings when it is unknown,
she brings when it is known.
phrases.notes: In other words, a doubtful bird חטאת and a definite one are the same kind of bird, so she can just switch it over.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes step 14's move: since the משנה now speaks of a woman who did not give birth, רב's 'וכיפר' is moved to the case of a woman who definitely gave birth.

steps.terutzMaskana: רב was speaking about a woman who learned she definitely gave birth, where atonement is natural.

steps.title: רב: after pinching, the bird atones and may be eaten
steps.stepSummary: If she found out after מליקה that she gave birth, רב rules the blood is put on the מזבח, she has atoned, and the bird may be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: If after the bird was pinched it became known that she gave birth, רב said: the כהן sprinkles its blood and squeezes out its blood, she has atoned, and it may be eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: This is רב's actual ruling. Once the bird was already pinched, finding out she definitely gave birth makes it a full, regular חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bird was killed as a doubtful חטאת, which normally is not eaten. רב says that since it turns out she really was obligated, it counts as a true חטאת from the start. So it brings atonement and is eaten by the כהנים like any normal bird חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: He sprinkles its blood on the wall of the מזבח
He squeezes out its blood against the מזבח
It atoned; she fulfilled her obligation
Permitted to be eaten (by the כהנים)

phrases.english: If after it was pinched
it became known that she gave birth,
Rav said: he sprinkles its blood
and squeezes out its blood, and it has atoned,
and it is permitted to be eaten.
phrases.notes: The letter ו in square brackets is added in the corrected wording; it just means "and."

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם מִשֶּׁנִּמְלְקָה נוֹדַע שֶׁיָּלְדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רב's ruling for the case set up in Step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After מליקה, if she learns she definitely gave birth, the blood is applied, she atones, and the bird may be eaten.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: forbidden to eat because of a decree
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees about eating: the bird is forbidden, so people won't think a doubtful bird חטאת may be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: it is forbidden to be eaten. This is a rabbinic decree, so people will not say that a bird חטאת brought out of doubt is eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the opposing view: the bird may not be eaten, even though the blood was put on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן does not argue that the bird is not a real חטאת. He worries only about how it looks. Onlookers saw it brought as a doubtful bird and won't know she later found out, so they might wrongly learn that doubtful birds may be eaten. So the חכמים forbade eating it.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made to prevent a mistake
Forbidden to be eaten
Lest people say: a worry about wrong conclusions

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a clear מחלוקת: רב says it is eaten, רבי יוחנן says it is not. Each side now gets a supporting ברייתא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: it is forbidden to be eaten,
a decree, lest people say:

phrases.aramaic: חַטַּאת הָעוֹף הַבָּאָה עַל הַסָּפֵק נֶאֱכֶלֶת.
phrases.english: a bird sin offering brought out of doubt is eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב's ruling in Step 16 about eating the bird.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bird may not be eaten, because of a rabbinic decree.

steps.title: Levi's baraita supports רב
steps.stepSummary: לוי teaches a ברייתא that matches רב: after מליקה, if she learns she definitely gave birth, the bird atones and may be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי taught like רב: a bird חטאת brought out of doubt, if after it was pinched it became known she definitely gave birth, the כהן sprinkles and squeezes out its blood, she has atoned, and it may be eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רב said, to show רב has a source behind him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording of לוי's ברייתא is almost the same as רב's words in Step 16. It clearly says the bird may be eaten, so it directly backs רב against רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with him, supporting his view

phrases.english: Levi taught in line with Rav:
a bird sin offering brought out of doubt,
if after it was pinched
it became known that she definitely gave birth,
he sprinkles its blood and squeezes out its blood,
and it has atoned, and it is permitted to be eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for רב's side of the מחלוקת.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that the bird may be eaten

steps.title: A baraita supporting רבי יוחנן begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא that supports רבי יוחנן. It first lists the cases where she finds out before מליקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught in line with רבי יוחנן: a bird חטאת brought out of doubt, if before it was pinched she found out she did not give birth, it becomes ordinary, or it may be sold to another woman. If before it was pinched she found out she definitely gave birth, it is made a definite חטאת, because the same kind she brings when unsure she brings when sure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a ברייתא supporting רבי יוחנן. These opening lines are setup about the before-מליקה cases; the line that actually supports רבי יוחנן (after מליקה) comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before מליקה, nothing has been done to the bird yet, so it can easily change status. If she did not give birth, it goes back to being ordinary, or it can be sold to another woman who needs a bird חטאת. If she did give birth, it simply becomes a definite חטאת. The after-מליקה case, where רבי יוחנן's view shows up, comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: It goes out to ordinary (non-holy) status
It may be sold to another woman who needs a bird חטאת

steps.confusionAlert: Nothing in these lines supports רבי יוחנן yet. All of them deal with before מליקה, which everyone agrees on. Wait for the after-מליקה line that follows.

phrases.english: It was taught in line with Rabbi Yochanan:
a bird sin offering brought out of doubt,
if before it was pinched
she found out that she did not give birth,
it goes out to ordinary status,
or it may be sold to her friend.
phrases.notes: "Her friend" means another woman who needs to bring a bird חטאת.

phrases.english: If before it was pinched
she found out that she definitely gave birth,
she should make it a definite sin offering,
because from the same kind she brings when it is unknown
she brings when it is known.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the support for רב, the גמרא brings a source for the other side, רבי יוחנן.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's ruling that the bird may not be eaten
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא whose relevant after-מליקה line comes next

steps.title: End of the ברייתא: after מליקה the bird is forbidden even for benefit
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא supporting רבי יוחנן finishes. If she finds out after מליקה that she gave birth, the bird is forbidden even for any benefit, since it came only for a doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: If, after the bird's neck was pinched, it became known that she definitely gave birth, the bird is forbidden even for benefit. It came from the start only because of a doubt; it atoned for that doubt, and the doubt is gone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא that backs up רבי יוחנן. This is the line that actually supports him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said the bird may be eaten. This ברייתא says the opposite: it may not even be used for benefit. The reason is that the bird was brought as a doubtful חטאת, and it stays under the rules of a doubtful bird even after the doubt is cleared up.

keyTerms.meaning: Benefit or use of any kind, not only eating
A doubt, an uncertain situation
It atoned
After its neck was pinched (the way a bird קרבן is slaughtered)

steps.whatToRemember: There is a ברייתא for each side. לוי's ברייתא matches רב (the bird may be eaten), and this ברייתא matches רבי יוחנן (it is forbidden, even for benefit).

phrases.english: If after it was pinched it became known that she gave birth –
it is forbidden even for benefit.
For it came from the start because of a doubt;
it atoned for her doubt, and it is gone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא that step 19 started quoting.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's ruling that the bird may not be eaten
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא ruling that after מליקה the bird is forbidden even for benefit, because it came only for a doubt

steps.title: New משנה: two rams bought for an אשם with two סלעים
steps.stepSummary: Someone set aside two סלעים for an אשם and bought two rams for an אשם. If one ram is worth two סלעים, it is offered. The other grazes until it gets a blemish, is sold, and its money goes to נדבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone set aside two סלעים for an אשם and used them to buy two rams for an אשם. If one of them is worth two סלעים, it is offered as his אשם. The second ram grazes until it gets a blemish; then it is sold, and its money goes to gift offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic. Money was set aside for an אשם, and it bought two rams for an אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם must be worth at least two סלעים. If one of the rams is worth that much, it can be his אשם. The second ram was bought with holy money, so it does not become ordinary. It waits until it gets a blemish, and then its money goes to gift offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
A coin worth four זוז; an אשם must be worth at least two of them
A guilt offering
It grazes until it gets a blemish
Gift offerings, paid for from leftover holy money

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the bird חטאת above. This is a brand new topic: money set aside for an אשם.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who sets aside two סלעים for an אשם
and bought with them two rams for an אשם –

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיָה אֶחָד מֵהֶן יָפֶה שְׁתֵּי סְלָעִים –
phrases.english: if one of them was worth two סלעים,
it is offered as his אשם,
and the second one grazes until it gets a blemish,
and it is sold, and its money goes to gift offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ram worth two סלעים is offered as the אשם. The extra ram grazes until it gets a blemish, and its sale money goes to נדבה.

steps.title: Both rams bought for ordinary use
steps.stepSummary: He used the אשם money to buy two rams for himself. The ram worth two סלעים is his אשם, and the second ram is for his מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he bought two rams for ordinary use with those coins, one worth two סלעים and one worth ten זוז, the one worth two סלעים is offered as his אשם, and the second is for his מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second version of the case. This time he spent the holy money on rams for his own use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using holy money for himself is מעילה, misuse of holy property, which requires an אשם מעילות plus repaying the money with a fifth added. The ram worth two סלעים is brought as his אשם for this מעילה. The second ram, worth ten זוז, takes care of his מעילה; the גמרא will explain exactly what that means.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary, non-holy use
Misusing holy property for yourself
A coin; four of them make one סלע

phrases.english: If he bought with them two rams for ordinary use,
one worth two סלעים
and one worth ten זוז –
phrases.notes: A סלע is four זוז, so ten זוז is a bit more than two סלעים.

phrases.english: the one worth two סלעים is offered as his אשם,
and the second one is for his מעילה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second version of the משנה's case: both rams were bought for ordinary use.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ram worth two סלעים is offered as his אשם, and the second ram covers his מעילה.

steps.title: One ram for an אשם and one for ordinary use
steps.stepSummary: He bought one ram as an אשם and one for himself. The אשם ram is offered, the second ram is for his מעילה, and he also pays one סלע plus a fifth.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one was bought for an אשם and one for ordinary use, and the אשם one is worth two סלעים, it is offered as his אשם. The second is for his מעילה, and he brings with it a סלע and its fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its third version of the case: a mix, with one ram bought for the אשם and one bought for himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ram bought as an אשם can be offered as long as it is worth two סלעים. The other ram takes care of his מעילה. Since only part of the holy money went to ordinary use, he pays back one סלע plus a fifth.

keyTerms.meaning: The extra fifth added when paying back holy property

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has three cases: both rams bought for an אשם, both bought for ordinary use, and one of each. Whenever he used holy money for himself, there is מעילה to take care of.

phrases.english: If one was for an אשם and one for ordinary use,

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיָה שֶׁל אָשָׁם יָפֶה שְׁתֵּי סְלָעִים –
phrases.english: if the אשם one was worth two סלעים,
it is offered as his אשם,
and the second one is for his מעילה,
and he brings with it a סלע and its fifth.
phrases.notes: He spent one of the two holy coins on himself here, so he pays back that one סלע plus a fifth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third version of the משנה's case: one ram of each kind.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The אשם ram worth two סלעים is offered, the second ram is for his מעילה, and he adds a סלע plus a fifth.

steps.title: What does 'his מעילה' mean in the first case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה means in the רישא when it says the second ram is 'for his מעילה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'his מעילה' that is taught in the first clause: 'and the second ram is for his מעילה'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה by asking what one word means. This question sets up the next few steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the רישא, the man bought two rams for himself with the אשם money. The ram worth two סלעים is his אשם, and the second ram goes 'for his מעילה.' The גמרא wants to know exactly what payment that second ram covers.

keyTerms.meaning: Wrongly using הקדש (holy property) for personal use
The first part of a משנה or ברייתא

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is "his misuse"
that is taught in the first clause:
"and the second one is for his misuse"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's analysis of the משנה cases quoted in Steps 21-23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What payment the word מעילתו refers to in the רישא.

steps.title: It cannot mean the אשם ram, because of the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: If מעילתו meant the אשם ram, the חומש would be paid together with the ram. But the פסוק shows the חומש is paid together with the stolen amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means the אשם ram, is that saying he brings the fifth together with the ram? But it is written: 'And what he sinned from the holy he shall pay, and he shall add its fifth to it.' This shows he brings the fifth together with what he stole!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one possible answer: 'his מעילה' means the אשם ram. Then it attacks that answer using a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the second ram were the אשם, the extra value of that ram would be paying the חומש. This would make the חומש go together with the קרבן. But the פסוק links the חומש to the repayment ('he shall pay... and add a fifth to it'), so the חומש goes with the stolen money, not with the ram.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (offering a possible answer that will be rejected)
The extra fifth added when repaying מעילה
The ram brought as a guilt offering
Evidently; this shows that
What he stole; here, the amount he took from הקדש

phrases.english: If we say it means the ram of the guilt offering,

phrases.aramaic: לְמֵימְרָא דְּחוֹמֶשׁ בַּהֲדֵי אַיִל מַיְיתֵי לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: is that to say he brings the fifth together with the ram?
But isn't it written:
"And that which he sinned from the holy, he shall pay,
and he shall add its fifth to it"?
Evidently he brings it together with what he stole!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests an answer to the question of Step 24 and immediately challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that מעילתו means the אשם ram.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading would attach the חומש to the קרבן, but the פסוק attaches the חומש to the repayment of the stolen amount.

steps.title: The סיפא also shows the חומש goes with the stolen amount
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא says he brings a סלע and its fifth together with the second ram, showing again that the חומש goes with the repayment.
steps.simpleTranslation: Also, the latter clause teaches: one ram for an אשם and one for himself. If the אשם ram is worth two סלעים, it is offered as his אשם, and the second is for his מעילה, and he brings with it a סלע and its fifth. This shows he brings the fifth together with what he stole!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second attack on the same suggestion, this time from the end of the משנה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the סיפא (Step 23), the second ram is 'for his מעילה,' and he adds a סלע plus a fifth. The fifth is paid alongside the repayment money, not alongside the קרבן. So the משנה itself treats the חומש as part of repaying what was taken.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore; a second challenge is coming
The last part of a משנה or ברייתא
Non-holy, ordinary property
A coin worth four זוז (דינרים)

phrases.english: And furthermore, the latter clause teaches:
one for a guilt offering and one for non-sacred use,

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיָה שֶׁל אָשָׁם יָפֶה שְׁתֵּי סְלָעִים –
phrases.english: if the one for the guilt offering was worth two sela,
it is offered as his guilt offering, and the second is for his misuse,
and he brings with it a sela and its fifth.

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא חוֹמֶשׁ בַּהֲדֵי גְּזֵילוֹ מַיְיתֵי לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: Evidently he brings the fifth together with what he stole!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge to the same suggestion attacked in Step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that מעילתו means the אשם ram.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא pairs the חומש with the repayment money, so the משנה itself does not attach the חומש to the קרבן.

steps.title: 'His מעילה' means repaying what he took from הקדש
steps.stepSummary: מעילתו means the repayment for the two סלעים he used from הקדש. The ten-זוז ram covers the stolen eight זוז plus the two-זוז fifth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, 'his מעילה' means what he benefited from הקדש: the two סלעים he set aside for an אשם and used to buy two rams for himself. The ram worth two סלעים he offers as the אשם ram, and the ram worth ten זוז he gives for what he benefited from הקדש, which is his stolen amount and its fifth. So what is 'his מעילה'? What he stole.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the first suggestion, the גמרא gives the real answer. 'His מעילה' means paying back what he took from הקדש, together with the fifth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He took two סלעים, which is eight זוז, from הקדש. Adding a fifth makes two more זוז, for ten in total. So the ram worth ten זוז pays back exactly the stolen amount plus its חומש, and the חומש goes with the repayment, just as the פסוק requires.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; introduces the correct answer after rejecting one
He benefited (from holy property)
Property belonging to the בית המקדש
A coin; four זוז make one סלע

steps.whatToRemember: מעילתו here does not mean the אשם קרבן. It means repaying what was taken from הקדש plus the חומש: two סלעים (eight זוז) plus a fifth (two זוז) equals ten זוז.
steps.confusionAlert: The word מעילה usually makes you think of the sin or the קרבן for it. Here the גמרא says it means the money owed back to הקדש.

phrases.english: Rather, "his misuse"
means what he benefited from consecrated property,
and that is the two sela
that he set aside for a guilt offering
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is the corrected spelling, so read it as 'he set them aside.'

phrases.english: and with them he bought two rams for non-sacred use.

phrases.aramaic: דְּיָפֶה שְׁתֵּי סְלָעִים מַקְרֵיב לֵיהּ אֵיל אָשָׁם,
phrases.english: The one worth two sela he offers as the guilt-offering ram,
and the one worth ten zuz he gives
for what he benefited from consecrated property,
which is his stolen amount and its fifth.
phrases.notes: Two sela are eight zuz, and a fifth added on top is two more, making ten.

phrases.english: So what is "his misuse"? What he stole.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected suggestion of Steps 25-26 with the correct meaning, answering the question of Step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מעילתו means the repayment of the stolen two סלעים plus the חומש, which the ten-זוז ram covers exactly.
steps.whyThisMatters: It keeps the משנה consistent with the פסוק: the חומש is always part of repaying הקדש, never part of the אשם קרבן.

steps.title: Recalling the רישא and quoting the סיפא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reminds us that מעילתו in the רישא was explained as גזילו, meaning the repayment. It then quotes the סיפא, where 'the second ram is for מעילה, and he brings a סלע and its fifth with it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: How did you explain 'his מעילה' in the first part of the משנה? As what he stole. Now look at the last part: one ram for the אשם and one for regular use. If the אשם ram is worth two סלעים, it is offered as his אשם. The second ram is for מעילה, and he brings with it a סלע and its fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up how it read the רישא and then quotes the סיפא. This is setup: it is getting ready to show a problem with that reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 27, מעילתו in the רישא meant the money owed back to הקדש (גזילו). In the סיפא, though, the second ram is called 'for מעילה' and the repayment (סלע and חומש) is listed separately. That makes 'מעילה' look like the name of the ram itself.

keyTerms.meaning: You explained it as / you set it up as
The first clause of the משנה
The last clause of the משנה
What he stole, meaning the amount he must pay back to הקדש
Regular, non-holy use
A סלע plus its added fifth

steps.confusionAlert: In the סיפא, the second ram was bought for regular use. Now it is being brought as the אשם for his מעילה, and the סלע plus fifth is the separate repayment.

phrases.english: How did you explain
'his מעילה' of the first clause? As what he stole.
phrases.notes: This points back to step 27, where מעילתו meant paying back the two סלעים.

steps.title: The same word seems to mean two different things
steps.stepSummary: From the סיפא it seems that מעילתו means the אשם ram. Yet the רישא uses מעילתו to mean the repayment. The גמרא starts to point out this mismatch.
steps.simpleTranslation: So clearly 'his מעילה' means the אשם ram. But the first clause calls the repayment 'his מעילה'...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the סיפא (מעילה means the ram) and begins to set it against the רישא (מעילה means the repayment). The contradiction continues in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the same משנה uses one word, it should mean one thing. Here the רישא seems to use מעילתו for the money paid back, and the סיפא seems to use it for the אשם ram. The גמרא is building a challenge out of this inconsistency.
